title: Bench capture probe - latency spike log
content:
Purpose:
Capture notes from the ad-hoc perf sync (2026-08-07) where we reproduced a new latency/throughput regression on the mixed-seq benchmark after recent batching heuristics changes. This is a working doc — rough notes, traces, hypotheses, and next steps.

Attendees (quick):
- Aisha (owner)
- Dmitry (batching heuristics)
- Sofia (observability + traces)
- Rafael (kv-cache, infra)
- Priya (oncall, joined for rollouts)

Summary of what we saw: (repro steps at bottom)
- Baseline (before change): mixed-seq baseline run (2026-07-25) p50=24ms, p95=172ms, p99=412ms, throughput ~610 qps @ bs=32, cpu/gpu util nominal.
- After heuristics tweak (PR #1427 rolled 2026-07-30): run on same hardware + model showed p95 jump to 420–480ms and p99 to 920–1,200ms across multiple shadow runs. Throughput dropped to ~420 qps for same offered load.
- Regression reproducible on canary pool (dedicated-qa-us-west) and in local cluster replay (k8s e2e). Not transient.

What changed in PR #1427 (short):
- We introduced a dynamic batching cutoff that tries to favour larger batches for requests estimated to be cheap (short seq) and avoid batching long sequences together to reduce tail latency. The estimator uses first-token model prompt-length heuristics + a new prefix-temperature heuristic.

Hypotheses (brainstorm):
1) Estimator misclassifies many mixed requests: several ~5% of requests are long seq (~>2048) but estimator marks them cheap early, so they get coalesced into large batches and cause KV cache thrashing / GPU kernel switching overhead.
2) Batching change reduced effective KV cache hits because previously similar prefixes were more often scheduled together; new scheduling mixes prefixes more, causing KV cache eviction churn.
3) Heuristic reduced warmup opportunities: fewer repeated small requests are grouped, so cold token-generation kernel path executed more often (higher setup cost).
4) Edge-case with quantized model path: when a batch contains a mix of quantized-compatible and non-compatible model variants we fall back to an expensive path. (unlikely but noted)

Data we captured during runs (representative):
- Run id: bench-run-2026-08-07-14:12
- Model: redwood/gpt-xxl-8k-qat (v2.1.3 pinned)
- Hardware: A100-80GB c5g-like private pool (dedicated-qa-us-west)
- Config: batch_limit=32, dynamic_batch_enabled=true (post-PR), kv_cache_prefetch=on, seq_dist: mean=128, median=96, 95th=1024, 99th=3072 (heavy tail), offered_load=650 qps
- Observed latency distribution (p50/p95/p99): 28ms / 460ms / 1050ms
- Throughput (sustained): 420 qps before backpressure kicks in
- KV cache hit rate sample (from addon trace): 74% (baseline was 92%)
- GPU kernel switch metric (new metric): average switches per second increased 3.6x in regression runs

Traces / evidence:
- Flame excerpt (trace id: trace-8-2026-08-07): shows a single batch of 28 requests including one long-seq (len 4096) request — GPU kernel path switched mid-batch causing tail amplification.
- Cache eviction logs (kv-evict-2026-08-07.log): repeated eviction of prefixes that were hot during baseline runs.
- Shadow-run comparison dashboard: diagnostic panel linked in Confluence (see linked_artifacts).

Immediate mitigation attempted (during sync):
- Hotfix rollback of dynamic batching estimator to the previous commit: rolled to canary midnight -> p95/p99 returned near baseline.
- Temporary rule: block batching across sequence_length_bucket boundaries (simple heuristic) while we investigate. This improved p99 but reduced throughput by ~5% compared to baseline (still better than regression).

Open questions / things to validate:
- What fraction of long requests are misclassified by the estimator? (Dmitry to add classification sampler)
- Does mixing quantized and non-quantized model variants occur in our cluster? (Rafael to check model routing logs)
- Could prefetching settings be causing more eviction churn? (Sofia + Rafael to run controlled A/B: prefetch on/off)
- Are there other recent changes (kernel selection fallback) that coincided? cross-check with release-engineering timeline.

Experiment plan (short-term):
1) Reproduce locally with a replay trace that injects heavy-tail sequences at the same 5% rate. We need deterministic harness to iterate. (owner: Aisha, target: 2026-08-10)
2) Add debug counters to estimator to record predicted "cheap" vs actual seq length and whether it's batched with long seqs. (owner: Dmitry, target: 2026-08-09)
3) Run A/B on canary: estimator v2 (current) vs estimator v2-guarded (block long seqs from being accepted into large batch). Measure p95/p99/throughput delta over 1 hour. (owner: Priya + SRE, target: 2026-08-11)
4) KV cache experiment: toggle prefetch and adjust eviction window, measure hit rate. (owner: Rafael, target: 2026-08-12)
5) Kernel-switch instrumentation: we need to capture per-batch kernel path transitions (Sofia to add lightweight probe). (owner: Sofia, target: 2026-08-09)

Longer-term (notes):
- Consider adding a batch-homogeneity score to the scheduler (score batches by variance of seq lengths + prefix hash similarity). Penalize high variance batches.
- Explore KV cache partitioning by tenant or prefix-hash to reduce cross-request eviction.

Repro steps (how to run the local replay):
- Use ./tools/replay --trace=heavy-tail-5pct.json --model=redwood/gpt-xxl-8k-qat:v2.1.3 --pool=local-gpu --clients=64 --rate=650 --batch_limit=32 --dynamic-batcher=true
- To run with diagnostic tracing: add --trace-out=trace-<id>.json and upload to trace viewer.
- Quick queries: curl http://obs-api.local/query?series=kv_cache_hit_rate&run=bench-run-2026-08-07

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- I suspect the estimator uses only first-token heuristics which are a bad proxy under heavy-context prompts (lots of system messages). Add tokenized-length estimate once we can sample first two tokens.
- The performance win that motivated the PR was real for short-only workloads; we need to preserve it without regressing mixed workloads.
- Danger: overly conservative fixes will kill throughput for our small-request PLG traffic — need to balance with per-route/tenant overrides.

Action items (owner, due):
- Dmitry: push classification counters + lightweight sampling log (due 2026-08-09)
- Sofia: add kernel-switch probe + dashboard panel (due 2026-08-09)
- Rafael: validate model routing mix and run KV prefetch toggle experiment on canary (due 2026-08-12)
- Priya: coordinate canary A/B schedule and rollback playbook (due 2026-08-10)
- Aisha: run local replay harness and collect trace-ids, compile short report (due 2026-08-10)

If you find anything in traces or quick checks, drop notes below and tag me in Slack (#eng-serving-runtime).

-- end of capture (working notes)
